blurb: Lonis Hamaili is a French-Algerian entrepreneur and independent investor who publishes under @_Lonis_ on X and at loniss.com. He is best known for his 'Cambrian Thesis,' a framework for trading public equities on short AGI timelines by identifying supply-chain bottleneck companies with high AI revenue concentration and low substitution risk. His work maps the AI infrastructure stack 15 layers deep — from raw materials through hyperscalers — assigning market-share, AI revenue, and operating-income metrics to each node. Outside of investing, Hamaili emerged from the Y Combinator S20 batch as co-founder of Dework, a Web3-native project-management and token-payments platform. He later co-founded Godmode (2023), an early consumer interface for agentic AI, and currently serves as VP of Growth at Próspera, a privately administered special economic zone in Honduras that replaces conventional municipal regulation with a contractual, insurance-backed governance model.
credibility_note: Hamaili explicitly labels his supply-chain mapping as personal research, not investment advice. His background is in venture-backed startups and city-building rather than institutional finance; he holds no known public investment-management credentials. AI revenue percentages attributed to individual companies in the map are his own approximations, not reported figures. Readers should assume he may hold positions in companies he discusses.
